Virtuous

VUR-choo-us -- stress on the first syllable, VUR. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Virtuous is righteous, moral, or ethical.

The mayor earned a reputation as virtuous by refusing every gift, favor, and shortcut offered to her office.

Worked Example

A student finds a wallet stuffed with cash, rides two buses across town to return it, and quietly turns down the reward the grateful owner presses on him.

Each choice in that chain is virtuous: doing the right thing because it is right, with no audience and no payoff. Virtuous describes people and conduct guided steadily by moral goodness.

How Virtuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

righteous

righteous: morally justified and good

upright

upright: strictly honorable and honest

honorable

honorable: honest, fair, and worthy of respect

Antonyms

corrupt

corrupt: willing to act dishonestly for gain

immoral

immoral: violating accepted moral standards

How Strong Is It? — honorable → righteous → virtuous

honorable vs. virtuous

honorable vs. virtuous: Honorable is solid but a shade milder than virtuous -- an honorable person keeps their word and plays fair, while a virtuous one holds every corner of life, seen and unseen, to the standard of goodness.

righteous vs. virtuous

righteous vs. virtuous: Righteous intensifies virtuous: a virtuous person quietly does what is moral, while a righteous one stands up for it as a cause -- a word so strong it can even tip into 'self-righteous' when the goodness starts performing for an audience.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of virtuous.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — virtu-

root — virtu-: moral excellence, worth, valor (Latin virtus 'virtue, excellence')

suffix — -uous

suffix — -uous: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Virtuous uses the -uous variant of this unit's suffix family (the u of the root virtus folds into the suffix's spelling). Latin virtus named excellence of character -- worth, valor, moral strength -- so virtuous means 'full of virtue': a person whose conduct is steadily righteous, moral, and ethical.

Use the root in a new word: virtuoso

Use the root in a new word: virtuoso: The virtuoso violinist earned three standing ovations before intermission.

Root Check

Word Choice

Virtuous judges character and conduct: a virtuous person, a virtuous choice, a virtuous life. Its noun is virtue, and the phrase 'a virtuous cycle' borrows the word for a loop where each good result feeds the next -- the cheerful opposite of a vicious cycle.
